Article Title: ios 27 public beta is out now: Siri AI, faster iPhones, and other features you should try first
Article Text:
Siri AI, which is finally a real assistant

The speed, which nobody has to opt into

Siri mode in the Camera

Clean Up, Extend and Spatial Reframing in Photos

Write with Siri, everywhere you type

Safari, which now builds its own extensions

Passwords that fix themselves

Liquid Glass, with a slider

Screen Time, rebuilt for parents

The rest, briefly

Should you install it?

Apple pushed the iOS 27 public beta out today, and for once the interesting part isn't buried in a footnote. Siri AI—the assistant Apple has been promising, delaying, apologising for and quietly rebuilding for the better part of two years—is finally in the hands of anyone willing to enrol a spare iPhone . September is still the official date. But the software is here now, it's unusually stable for a first public build, and there's enough in it to justify the risk on a secondary device.That's the caveat worth repeating before anything else. This is beta software. It will eat battery. Some apps will break. Back up first, and don't put it on the phone you need working tomorrow morning. If you can live with that, here's what's actually worth opening first.Start here, because everything else in iOS 27 is downstream of it. Siri has been rebuilt around Apple's next-generation Apple Intelligence stack, and it now behaves like a chatbot rather than a command parser. You can hold a back-and-forth conversation. You can ask a follow-up without restating the whole question. It searches the web when it needs to.The part that separates it from ChatGPT or Claude isn't raw capability—it's access. Siri has private, on-device reach into your messages, emails, photos, notes, calendar and reminders. Ask it to find the restaurant your friend recommended three months ago in a text thread you can't remember, and it will actually go looking.Ask it to add every ingredient from a recipe page to your shopping list. Tell it to lock all the doors at midnight and it builds the home automation. It can delete files, add a birthday to a contact, pull a password out of the Passwords app, recommend a place to eat based on what it already knows about you.Responses surface from the Dynamic Island, and pulling down on one opens the full conversation. There's also a standalone Siri app now, syncing your history privately through iCloud, so a question you start on iPhone can be picked up on iPad. You can pin conversations. You can start fresh.The compatibility list is where it gets restrictive. Siri AI needs an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone, which means iPhone 15 Pro or newer. It launches in English only, it won't be available in the EU at the start, and you may hit a waitlist before you get in. Some of the more advanced on-device work is gated further still, to iPhone 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max and iPhone Air.Here's the thing most reviews will underplay: the best feature in iOS 27 has nothing to do with AI, and it works on an iPhone 11.Apple optimised the CPU scheduler all the way back through the supported lineup, and the difference is immediate. Apps launch up to 30% faster. New photos land in your library up to 70% faster. AirDrop transfers between nearby devices finish up to 80% faster. But the numbers undersell it—what you notice is that animations are quicker, the keyboard opens without hesitation, App Library doesn't stutter, Home Screen pages swap cleanly, unlocking feels instant. Camera even launches faster in Low Power Mode.iMessage sync between devices is more accurate, and failed messages now retry automatically instead of sitting there with a red exclamation mark. Your iPhone also stops clinging to a dying Wi-Fi network as you walk out of the house; the handoff to cellular is smarter. Search has been rebuilt across Spotlight, Photos and Mail, and Mail now surfaces up to five ranked Top Results, which finally makes finding a buried email a two-second job.None of this requires Apple Intelligence. None of it requires new hardware. It's the update everyone gets.Visual Intelligence has been in iOS for a while. What's changed is that it's now a mode in the Camera app, sitting alongside photo and video, which means it takes one tap to reach instead of a hunt through the interface.Point it at a dish and Siri will give you nutritional information. Point it at a receipt and it will work out who owes what. Photograph a loyalty or membership card and it turns into a Wallet pass. Snap a flyer and it can import the event straight into Calendar. It also works on what's already on your screen—summarise an article, search an image, ask a question about the page you're reading.Three tools, and the third is the interesting one. Clean Up has been rebuilt to handle larger and messier removals, filling in what's behind the object far more convincingly than the version that shipped last year. Extend generates content beyond the existing frame, which is the fix for every photo you cropped too tight in the moment.Spatial Reframing is the one to test first, though. It lets you move the viewpoint, adjust the angle or zoom in after the shot is taken—as if you were repositioning the camera retroactively. Feed it a portrait with an awkward composition and see how far it can push before it falls apart. That's the honest test of whether this is a tool or a party trick.Siri can now generate text from scratch, system-wide, from the keyboard. Describe what you need in plain language and it drafts. It'll also give you feedback on something you've already written, change the tone, tighten the wording.The genuinely useful bit is confined to Messages and Mail, where Siri analyses your existing correspondence and matches your writing style, punctuation and tone. Proofreading now runs automatically as you type, catching grammar as well as spelling.Two things here. The first is organisational: Safari can automatically group your tabs by topic, group bookmarks and Reading List items, and surface recently closed topics on the Start Page. Notify Me will watch a page and alert you when something changes—a price drop, a restock.The second is stranger and more interesting. You can create a custom Safari extension by describing it in a sentence. Apple's own examples are telling: create a citation for the current page and copy it to the clipboard, set a minimum font size of 14pt, style websites like they're from the nineties, highlight and show the dimensions of page elements when you tap them, enter design mode so you can edit a page's contents. Turn the page into pirate speak, if you must.The Passwords app already told you which of your credentials were weak or compromised. In iOS 27 it does something about them—it uses Safari to go and change them on your behalf, handling verification codes and showing progress in a Live Activity. It needs an Apple Intelligence-capable device. It is, arguably, the single most quietly valuable feature in the release.Shortcuts, made approachableIf Shortcuts has always felt like a programming environment you didn't ask for, iOS 27 fixes the on-ramp. Describe what you want—"when I'm leaving work, message Pedro that I'm on my way with my ETA"—and Shortcuts builds the automation, connecting actions across apps. You can then refine it with further natural-language requests, or drop into manual editing if you'd rather.Calendar gets the same treatment. Describe an event and it creates it. Change a lunch meeting to a coffee chat and it adjusts the details.Apple hasn't walked back last year's redesign. It's made it adjustable. Controls now diffuse busy backgrounds more effectively, darker edges and brighter highlights create better separation, and app icons carry more layers and definition. Readability was the complaint; readability is the fix.The new bit is a slider under Settings > Appearance, running from ultra-clear to fully tinted, applying across iOS and third-party apps alike. Worth noting: at least one reviewer who went in expecting to love the most translucent setting ended up parked at the fully opaque end.This is the largest overhaul in the release that has nothing to do with AI. A new dashboard gives parents a clear view of a child's usage with one-tap access changes. Time Allowances set limits per category—Games, Entertainment, Social Media—with Apple offering age-based guidance developed with clinical and child development experts, which parents can override. Schedules control which apps are available at which times, so school days, evenings and weekends can each get their own routine.Ask to Browse extends the Ask to Buy model to the web: children request permission for new sites, parents approve or decline from Messages. Kids can also be required to ask before contacting someone new. Communication Safety, which already blurs nudity in Messages and FaceTime, now intervenes on gore and violent content too.One catch, and it matters: the redesigned experience only works if every participating Family Sharing device is on the OS 27 generation.Custom EQ arrives for AirPods 4, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Max 2, letting you tune lows, mids and highs. HomeKit Secure Video cameras support 4K recording and get AI-generated descriptions of what happened, plus natural-language clip search—the AI parts need a 2TB iCloud+ plan at launch, the 4K doesn't. Shared Albums finally support full-resolution sharing and let people on Android and Windows contribute via iCloud. com. iPhone connects directly to GymKit-compatible cardio equipment. FaceTime shoots front and rear cameras simultaneously on iPhone Air and the iPhone 17 line. Alarm volume is now independent of system volume, which somehow took until 2026.If you have a spare iPhone, yes—this is one of the more stable first public betas Apple has shipped, and Siri AI is the most consequential change to the iPhone's software in years. If you only have one phone and you need it to work, wait for September. Apple is still refining Siri, still fixing bugs, still tweaking features, and the Feedback Assistant app exists for a reason.But the pitch here isn't really Siri. It's that Apple spent a year making the iPhone faster on hardware it sold you five generations ago, and then built the AI on top of that. Of the two, the first one is harder to do.
Article Summary: Apple pushed the iOS 27 public beta out today, and for once the interesting part isn't buried in a footnote. Siri AI is finally in the hands of anyone willing to enrol a spare iPhone. Apple optimised the CPU scheduler all the way back through the supported lineup, and the difference is immediate. Siri has been rebuilt around Apple's next-generation Apple Intelligence stack.
